transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just can’t shake this feeling that I’m a danger to people and a disappointment. There was this near-miss, and it’s like my mind keeps using it as proof that I’m not meant to be a nurse. I keep thinking everyone would be better off without me around.
How long have you been feeling this way about being a danger and a disappointment?
About a year and two months now. It started after I graduated high school, when I began college classes and working full-time at the clinic.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Not really. I used to jog to clear my head, or knit, cook, read after class… things like that. Now I usually just end up sitting on my bed still in my scrubs, and I can’t make myself care enough to do any of it.
Have you noticed any change in your ability to experience pleasure or enjoy things you used to find enjoyable over the past year?

Yes. I mean, I used to actually enjoy things after class—jogging, knitting, cooking, reading. They helped me feel like myself. Now I just end up sitting on my bed in my scrubs, and I can’t make myself care enough to do any of it.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in almost all activities most of the time over the past year?

Yes. Most of the time I just don’t want to do anything. I used to jog, knit, cook, or read after class to clear my head, but now I usually just sit on my bed in my scrubs and can’t make myself care about any of it.
Have you had thoughts of death or dying repeatedly over the past year?
Yes… not like I have a plan to hurt myself. But I do keep having thoughts like it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or if I could disappear so I wouldn’t mess anything up again.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt better, with little to no depressive symptoms, at any point over the past year?

No, not really. It’s been pretty continuous. This started about a year and two months ago, after I graduated high school and started college classes and working full-time at the clinic, and I haven’t had a couple weeks where I felt back to normal.
Have you had any periods, even if just a few days, where your depressive feelings significantly lifted over the past year?

Not really. I mean, maybe I’ve had a better day here or there, but nothing where it really lifted. It’s felt like this pretty steadily since after high school, when I started college classes and working full-time at the clinic… so, about a year and two months now.
Has this feeling of being a danger and a disappointment, along with the loss of interest in activities, been going on for more than two years now?
No… it hasn’t been more than two years. It’s been about a year and two months, since after I graduated high school and started college classes and working full-time at the clinic.
Have you had any periods, regardless of how short, where you felt completely back to your normal self over the past year?

No, I don’t think so. Maybe there have been moments or a day that felt a little easier, but I haven’t felt completely like myself again. It’s been going on since after I graduated high school and started college and working full-time at the clinic, so about a year and two months.
Are there any specific situations, people, or events that make you feel more depressed or trigger these feelings of being a danger and a disappointment?

Yeah… it’s mostly work-related. That near-miss I had really set it off. Since then, anytime I’m at the clinic or even thinking about being a nurse, I start feeling like I’m dangerous somehow, like I’m going to hurt someone. And then it turns into feeling like I’m just a disappointment, like maybe I’m not meant to do this and people would be better off without me.
Have you had any period, no matter how brief, where these feelings of being a danger, a disappointment, and the loss of interest in activities significantly improved over the past year?
Not really, no. It’s been pretty steady since after I graduated high school and started college classes and working full-time at the clinic… so, about a year and two months now.
Are there any specific situations or events outside of work that make you feel more depressed or trigger these feelings of being a danger and a disappointment?

Outside of work, not really anything specific. It mostly comes back to that near-miss and what it makes me think about myself. Even when I’m not at the clinic, I’ll remember it and start feeling like it proves I’m dangerous, like I’m a disappointment and maybe I shouldn’t be a nurse.
Have you had a period of at least two months where you felt significantly better and your depressive symptoms were much less bothersome?

No, I don’t think so. It’s been going on pretty consistently for about a year and two months, since I finished high school and started college classes and working full-time at the clinic. I haven’t really had a two-month stretch where it felt much better.
Has your current episode of depression lasted for more than two years?
No, not more than two years. It’s been about a year and two months, since after I graduated high school and started college classes and working full-time at the clinic.
Have you had more than one episode of depression like this in your lifetime?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve had another time like this before, at least not that I can clearly point to. This feels like the main time it’s been this bad.
Have you ever felt this way before this episode started about a year and two months ago?
Not really, no. I mean, I’d had normal stressful or sad times before, but nothing that felt like this or lasted like this.
Have you had an episode of depression like this before the one that started about a year and two months ago?
I don’t think so. I’ve had rough periods before, but not anything like this episode or something I’d call the same.
Have you had any other episodes of depression before this one that started a year and two months ago?
No, not that I can think of. I’ve had bad days or stressful times before, but I wouldn’t say I had another episode like this before.
Have you experienced an episode of depression similar to this one before in your life?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve had times where I was upset or stressed, but nothing that really felt similar to this.
